title: Sharp Value Bounds for Two-Stage Incremental Policies Responding to Counterfactual Histories
banked_reason: D0.5.G: paper_score_ceiling 6.7 < 7.4, so the delivered field tier is capped at subfield; finite common-history scope, no substantive application, and no implemented confidence-projection demonstration.
gap_reasons: The paper’s practical significance is constrained by its finite common-history support assumption and by the absence of an application establishing that assumption for a substantive counterfactual history.
The confidence projection has a coverage proof, but its certified computation is specified through exhaustive subdivision or unspecified exact extrema, with no implemented demonstration.

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved attained sharp bounds for the intervention-induced-history target, finite-support primal/dual and sorting formulas, simultaneous completion, and the exact identification frontier; decision and math review passed with all citations attested. The result remained at subfield because its common-history scope lacked a substantive application and its confidence projection had no implemented demonstration. Reaching field would require a separately re-anchored broader history-space and applied project.
tldr: The sharp value of a two-decision incremental policy is derived when its second decision responds to the potential history \(Z(a)\) created under the first decision. For bounded real outcomes and finite histories, explicit counterfactual-law completion and an antitone outcome coupling give attained endpoints and an exact point-identification frontier under the original outcome-marginal sensitivity model. With finite outcome support, the same endpoints have a finite hinge dual, a sorted linear-arithmetic formula, and a tie-valid confidence projection.
gap: Existing static-regime sensitivity results do not determine the joint \((Z(a),Y(a,0),Y(a,1))\) needed for a genuinely dynamic policy. The motivating two-period preprint uses a displayed observed-history weight and leaves computation open; its literal objective fails a constant-outcome normalization check.
fill: Prove full-law completion, reduced-program and hinge/max dual equality, the simultaneous CDF-dominance reduction, a sorting endpoint, the exact collapse boundary, and tie-valid certified confidence projection.
